sentences.text: This petition under Section 166 Motor Vehicles Act 1989 is filed seeking compensation of .10,00,000/- for the death of Ramigani Ramachandra Reddy S/o Ramigani Ramanna, in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated in the petition that on 28-04- 2023, at about 6.50 AM., Ramigani Ramachandra Reddy was walking as a pedestrian on the left side of Gurramakonda main road, at Ramiganipalle village,
Kurubalakote Mandal, Andhra Pradesh.

At that time, the driver of a private Bus bearing No.AP-39-W-4856 (herein after called as alleged offending vehicle) was driving at a high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, and hit Ramigani Ramachandra Reddy.
As a result of the accident, he fell down, sustained body all over his body and died on the spot.
After postmortem was conducted at District hospital, Madanapalle, deceased's body was handed over to the petitioner.

The Petitioner has stated that she spent .2,00,000/- for the transportation of the dead body, funeral and obsequies ceremonies etc.
3.
It is further stated that the accident and death solely due to negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
At the time of accident, deceased was 77 years, working as an agriculturist and coolie, earning .20,000/- p.m.
The Petitioner, being the wife of the deceased, financially dependent on his income.
It is requested to award .30,00,000/- compensation with interest from the Respondent No.1 and 2 being the insurer and insured of the offending vehicle.
4. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.1 has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and filed the written statement.
The Respondent No.2 has not appeared before the court and he was placed exparte.
5. Respondent No.1-Insurance company, has admitted to issuing an insurance policy in respect of offending vehicle.
However, it has stated that its liability is subjected to terms and conditions of the said policy.
6. The respondent no 1 has denied the negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle and has contended that the accident occurred due to negligence of the deceased.
It stated that since the deceased was 77 years old and crossing the road without observing oncoming vehicular traffic, a greater degree of contributory negligence lies with the deceased.
7. The respondent no 1 has further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess a valid DL and offending vehicle had no valid FC and permit.
It has also denied all the allegations regarding the age, avocation and income of the deceased as well as petitioner's dependency on him.

It has also asserted that compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant and prayed for dismissal of the petition.
8.

On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues have been framed :-
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that the death of Ramigani Ramachandra Reddy S/o.Ramigani Ramanna was only due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of private Bus bearing No.AP-39-W-4856 on 28-04-2023 about 6.50 a.m. at Ramigani Narayanamma vs National Ins Co Ltd on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179661497/
2 Ramiganipalle village, on Gurramakonda Madanapalle Main Road, Kurubalakote Mandal, Andhra Pradesh District?
2. What compensation Petitioner is entitled?
3. What order?
9.

sentences.text: In support of the claim, Petitioner is examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.11.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.1 has not chosen to adduce any oral and documentary evidence.
10. I heard the counsel on both sides and have perused the material on record .

11. By considering the evidence and materials available on record and after hearing the arguments my findings to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative. Issue No.2: Partly In the Affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 12. ISSUE NO.1:-

Petitioner says that on 28-04- 2023, at about 6.50 AM., Ramigani Ramachandra Reddy was walking as a pedestrian on the left side of Gurramakonda main road, at Ramiganipalle village, Kurubalakote Mandal, Andhra Pradesh.
At that time, the driver of offending vehicle was driving at a high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, and hit Ramigani Ramachandra Reddy.
As a result of the accident, he fell down, sustained body all over his body and died on the spot.
Petitioner says that it was the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
she relied on the police records and submitted that the police have filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle and it is requested to award compensation from the respondents.

13. In support of her version Petitioner has produced FIR, Complaint, PM report, inquest report,
IMV report and Charge sheet at Ex.P1 to 7.
14.
To prove the negligence on the part driver of the offending vehicle, Petitioner examined herself as PW-1 and she relied on the police records.
During the course of cross examination, suggestion was put to PW1 that the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of the deceased and not on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
PW.1 has denied this suggestion.
She also denied that the deceased was over 70 years and that he suffered from visual and hearing impairments.
She further denied that the accident could have been avoided had her husband looked either side before the incident.
Further she denied that allegation that the deceased had come into contact with the bus on his own.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the respondent has vehemently argued that driver of the offending vehicle was driving the offending bus slowly and cautiously on the left side of his direction, the deceased had come into contact with the bus on his own., which resulted in accident.
He further argued that the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of rider of the deceased and not on the part of driver of the offending vehicle.
Thereby the respondent is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.
16. Keeping in view of contention raised by the parties once again I perused the material available on record.
Police have filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle.
There is no material on record to disprove the Petitioner's evidence and to prove the contention of the Respondent.
The evidence of PW-1 corroborates with the documents produced.
There is nothing elicited to disprove the case of the petitioner.

It is well settled principle that Motor Vehicles Act is beneficial legislation,
the tribunal need not to go for the strict proof of rash and negligence.
After the investigation, police have filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle and the copy of the charge sheet is produced at Ex.P.7.
Charge sheet prima-facie establishes the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
From all the above materials clearly indicate that the accident was due to the negligence of driver of offending vehicle.
Based on the entire records, I hold that the driver of offending vehicle was negligent in causing the accident due to which Ramigani Ramachandra Reddy died due to injuries sustained in the RTA.
Hence, this Issue is answered in the Affirmative.
17. Issue No.2:
The Petitioner states that she is the wife and legal heir of the deceased R.Ramachandra Reddy.
She has produced Aadhaar cards at Ex.P.9 to 10, which clearly indicates that deceased was the husband of Petitioner.
Hence, I hold that the Petitioner is the legal representative of the deceased and she is entitled for compensation as dependent.

During the course of cross-examination PW-1 has stated that she and deceased have 4 children, and they got married and are residing separately.
18.
It is stated that the deceased R.Ramachandra Reddy deceased was 77 years, working as an agriculturist and coolie, earning .20,000/- p.m.

The Petitioner, being the wife of the deceased,
financially dependent on his income.
To prove the occupation and income, the Petitioner has not produced any documents.
To prove the occupation and income, the Petitioners have not produced any documents.
In the absence of proof of income, this tribunal is of the opinion that the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
Since the accident has been occurred in the year 2023, notional income Rs.16,000/- per month is taken for the assessment of compensation.

19. The PW-1 has produced Ex.P.10- Aadhaar card of deceased, which shows the birth year of deceased as 1945 and considering the same, he was aged 78 years as on the date of accident and proper multiplier applicable to the case is 5.
As the age of the deceased is above 60 years, no future prospects is to be added.

As there are only one dependent,  of the income is to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses and the annual income would come to (Rs.8,000 X 12)
Rs.96,000/- and applying 5 multiplier, Petitioners are awarded Rs.4,80,000/- towards loss of dependency.

sentences.text: CONSORTIUM:

By following the guidelines of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs- Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Others., this Tribunal deems it proper to hold that the Petitioner is entitled .44,000/- under the head of consortium as she has lost her husband.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 21. Loss to estate:
It appears that the Petitioner has lost her husband.
Hence, .20,000/- is awarded towards loss to estate.
22. Funeral Expenses:
Petitioner has claimed that they have spent .2,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral & obsequies ceremony expenses.
By considering the facts and circumstances it would be proper to award .16,500/- for the funeral and other incidental expenses.

23. In all, the amount of compensation awarded by this Tribunal to the Petitioner under various headings is as follows :
Sl.No Nature of Compensation Amount 1. Loss of dependency Rs. 4,80,000/-
2. Loss of consortium Rs. 44,000/-
to Petitioners 3. Loss to estate Rs. 20,000/-
4. Transportation of Rs. 16,500/-
dead body, Funeral & obsequies Expenses Total Rs. 5,60,500/-
24.
Liability:
The Petitioner has lead cogent evidence and has proved that the accident was occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle.
The policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Hence the Respondent No.1 and 2 being the insurer and insured of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
However, in view of the issuance policy, the Respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner with interest at 6% per annum.
With these observations, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
25. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with cost.
 Petitioner is awarded  compensation of Rs.5,60,500/-
